messages:
alice_cust: Hi, we're seeing a bunch of requests from EU users suddenly routed to us-east (extra 250-400ms). Response headers show `x-region: us-east-1`. This started ~08:10 UTC. Anycast/GeoDNS issue? :thinking:

maria_support: Sorry for the hit — can you share a sample request ID + timestamp and a curl output? Also which domain are you hitting (api.redwood.ai or custom domain)?

alice_cust: Account: acme-inc. Sample curl and headers below (08:12 UTC):

```
$ curl -s -D - https://api.redwood.ai/health -o /dev/null
HTTP/2 200\ncontent-type: application/json\ncontent-length: 123\nx-region: us-east-1\nx-request-id: rq_202403081212_abc123\n
```

We usually get `x-region: eu-west-1` from our Frankfurt users. DNS lookup from a EU client: `dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1` -> `34.195.12.8` (an us-east IP).

maria_support: Thanks — that's useful. We're going to try to reproduce. Two quick asks: 1) can you run `dig +trace api.redwood.ai` from the affected client and paste results? 2) have you recently set any custom CNAMEs or TTLs on your side?

alice_cust: Paste of `dig +trace` from home ISP (08:15 UTC):

```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +trace api.redwood.ai
...
;; Received 1 answers, 0 authority records, 1 additional records
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 34.195.12.8
api.redwood.ai. 300 IN A 34.195.13.7
```

TTL is 300 on our side. No custom CNAMEs.

jon_infra: Quick theory: our geo-steering mapping is returning the us-east anycast IP for that prefix for some EDNS/ISP-subnet combos. Also possible: the authoritative DNS TTL was recently increased and some resolvers are still serving older records. Can you check `dig @8.8.8.8 +short api.redwood.ai` from both EU and NA hosts? That helps show resolver differences.

alice_cust: Got both: EU (Frankfurt) -> `34.195.12.8`; NA (NY) -> `34.195.12.8` as well (same).

ops_geo: Paging infra/network — @jon_infra @tim_netops. This looks like a geoip->ip mapping mismatch. Two possibilities: 1) our global load-balancer recently had a partial config push causing a US-preferring fallback for certain prefixes; 2) an upstream DNS provider (or CDN) did a propagation with new anycast IP range that maps to US locations.

jon_infra: Good call. I pulled the RDNS table for that prefix: the allocation is announced from both regions but the BGP origin for that exact IP currently has better path to our us-east POP. Also seen similar reports from another customer ~10m ago. Action: rolling back the last POP mapping change and lowering authoritative TTL to 60 for the next 15m to accelerate convergence.

maria_support: For customer repro: if you want to force EU routing while we fix infra, try `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:REGION_EU_IP https://api.redwood.ai/health` replacing REGION_EU_IP with a eu-west IP from our list. That will validate client-side behavior.

alice_cust: Tried `--resolve` with the eu ip — request hits eu and latency drops to 20ms. OK that proves routing is the issue. Any ETA on rollback?

tim_netops: Rolling back POP mapping now. Also resetting authoritative DNS TTL to 60. Note: some ISPs still cache answers regardless of TTL (ISP-level caching) — if they have cached the previous A answer, it might take up to their cache lifetime. We're contacting the DNS provider to request cache purge for the affected records.

srebot: Incident created: INC-2025-847. Owner: jon_infra. Priority: P2. Linked to config change: POP-mapping-2025-03-08.

jon_infra: Rollback applied at 08:28 UTC. Please test. We'll keep TTL low for 30 mins then raise back to 300. Also added a temporary health-check based fallback so eu nodes prefer eu IPs even if load slightly higher.

alice_cust: Re-tested at 08:33 UTC — EU clients now showing `x-region: eu-west-1` and latency back to normal. Thanks.

maria_support: Glad that's fixed. Follow-ups: we'll keep monitoring for 1h, and ops will perform a postmortem on why the mapping push affected EDNS clients. For you: if you want to avoid transient cross-region routing, you can set `region: eu-west-1` in your request header or pin to a dedicated endpoint (Dedicated/Private customers).

alice_cust: Appreciate it. Any guidance on TTL best practices? We use a TTL=300 but maybe lower?

tim_netops: For geo-sensitive endpoints, keep authoritative TTL=60 during high-change windows. For stable production, 300-600 is OK. Also try to avoid long-living CNAME chains; some resolvers cache A records from CNAMEs and extend caching beyond TTL.

maria_support: Closing the ticket here once we confirm monitoring stable. If you see a recurrence, please reopen INC-2025-847 or ping this thread. :thumbsup:
